title: UniFi Network
description: Gateways, switches, access points and clients at both sites, polled from the UniFi consoles by unpoller.

panels.title: Console reachable
panels.description: unpoller's view of each console. 0 means the poll is failing.

panels.title: WAN IP
panels.description: Public address on each gateway's WAN port. Both are static today and several things assume that, so a change here matters.

panels.title: Internet latency — both sites
panels.description: Console's own reachability probe to the internet.

panels.title: WAN utilisation against provisioned line rate
panels.description: Throughput as a share of what the ISP sells. The provisioned rate comes from the console's own WAN config, so it tracks a plan change.

panels.title: WAN interface errors and drops
panels.description: Interface-level counters on the WAN port. This is not ISP path loss — unpoller exposes no such metric. Reachability is covered by the London watchdog instead.

panels.title: Speedtest
panels.description: The console's own periodic speedtest, not a continuous measurement.

panels.title: Temperature
panels.description: Bristol was at 83 °C when the kit was inventoried, which is worth watching rather than reacting to.

panels.title: Firmware
panels.description: An upgradable device is not urgent, but a device on a much older release than its peers is worth a look.

panels.title: Channel utilisation per radio
panels.description: Airtime in use. A radio sitting high here is congested regardless of how few clients it has.

panels.title: Client transmit rate — the WiFi ceiling
panels.description: Negotiated PHY rate per client. This is the panel that would have shown the ~30 Mbps ceiling behind the 33.8 Mbps Plex remux stutter. Real throughput is roughly half the PHY rate.

panels.title: Client signal
panels.description: Anything below about -70 dBm will be negotiating a low rate.

panels.title: Transmit retries per radio
panels.description: Rising retries with steady client counts means interference.

panels.title: Port link speed
panels.description: A port that has renegotiated down shows up here before anyone notices it as slowness.

panels.title: LAG member throughput
panels.description: The two LAG members individually. A single TCP flow cannot exceed one member, so a large transfer tops out at 1 Gbps even with both legs up.

panels.title: LAG utilisation against the 2 Gbps ceiling
panels.description: The 10G spine reaches the rest of the LAN through 2 Gbps. Traffic that stays on the aggregation switch is unaffected; anything north-south shares this.

panels.title: LAG members up
panels.description: Two. If this reads 1 the capacity has silently halved and every other panel still looks healthy.

panels.title: Per-member link speed
panels.description: 1 Gbps per member is the ceiling: the Loft Switch's SFP ports are 1G only, so this is the hardware limit, not a fault.

panels.title: Member balance
panels.description: Both members carrying traffic means the hash is spreading flows. Sustained traffic on one leg only means it is pinning them.

panels.title: PoE draw against switch budget
panels.description: Against the switch's own PoE budget — 95 W on the Loft Switch. Filtered to switches that supply PoE, so the aggregation switch is absent by design rather than missing.

panels.title: Clients by band
panels.description: Band labels are the console's own: ng is 2.4 GHz, na is 5 GHz.

panels.title: Top talkers
panels.description: Combined receive and transmit rate, wired and wireless.
